Definition: from G303 and a derivative of G2537; to restore:--renew.
BiblicalUsage: The word appears once, in the warning of Hebrews 6: if they shall fall away, it is impossible to renew them again unto repentance, seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh. It is the renewing that cannot happen twice — the one who has tasted the heavenly gift and turned away cannot be made new again by the same repentance.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for renewing again carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the warning — a renewal that, once thrown away, cannot simply be repeated.
